> 鼎。元吉，亨。

Hexagram 50 is about a bronze vessel, and the 彖's first sentence says the hexagram is the vessel.

## 鼎，象也 — the hexagram is a picture of the thing

鼎 is a pictograph: three legs, two ears, one belly. In the oracle bones it is a drawing of the object.

And 彖's opening sentence, 鼎，象也, has two readings: 象 as "image of the vessel" (the hexagram's lines depict a 鼎), or 象 as "symbol" (the 鼎 symbolizes dynastic power).

This book takes the first, and the correspondence is exact:

- 初六, one yielding line at the bottom: the legs
- 九二, 九三, 九四, three solid lines: the belly
- 六五, yielding in the middle of the top: the ears
- 上九, solid at the top: the carrying bar

So 象也 is literal. The hexagram is named 鼎 because it looks like a 鼎.

The symbolic sense grows out of that, and the two readings do not conflict.

## 顛趾，出否

初六 鼎顛趾，利出否.

倒 the vessel over, feet up: 顛趾.
出否: pour out what is stale and foul.

The first act of a new vessel is to turn it upside down and empty it, before anything is put inside.

## 餗

餗 is the food in the 鼎.

九四 鼎折足，覆公餗，其形渥，凶.

The leg breaks, the duke's food is spilled, and 其形渥 — the shape soaked, dripping, disgraced.

(A variant reading in the 周禮 commentary tradition has 其刑剭, a heavy punishment. Two readings, a large gap: one is humiliation, one is conviction. This book keeps both and uses 形渥 in the text, because the 象 immediately asks 信如何也 — what of your credibility — which is about reputation, not penalty.)

## 鉉

鉉 is the bar passed through the two ears to carry the vessel. 說文 鉉，舉鼎具也.

However heavy the 鼎, it needs one bar through both ears before it can be lifted.

## 黃耳，金鉉

六五 鼎黃耳，金鉉，利貞.

Yellow ears, metal bar. Both are the middle: colour of the centre, and a bar of the hardest material.

The line does not add capacity. It makes the vessel liftable.

## 雉膏

A fat pheasant, the richest dish in the vessel.

九三 鼎耳革，其行塞，雉膏不食 — the ear is altered, the movement blocked, and the good food goes uneaten.

方雨虧悔，終吉 — when the rain comes the regret diminishes, and in the end it is good.

Rain here is the meeting of yin and yang: the fire has been too strong, and a rain adjusts it.

## 正位凝命

The 象: 君子以正位凝命.

正: to set straight. 凝: to fix, to gather and not scatter.

Not "hold the position." Set the position straight, and fix the mandate onto this vessel.

Position is outside; the mandate is inside. When the position is true, the mandate can settle.

## The test

Take an institution or a household you have inherited. Ask the first line's question before any other: has the vessel been turned upside down and emptied? And then the fourth: which is the leg that would break under the weight, and would anyone still trust the food in it.
